new.name: S2-3b
new.text:
# Term-by-term: regress EACH "tougher terms" flag on cause (year + industry FE, clustered by company).
# This is the most direct test of lender screening -- the index above just sums these.
rows = []
for f in ["haircut_any", "equitized", "equity_control", "governance", "docs_tight", "docs_loose",
          "nm_priming", "extension_any", "pik", "sponsor_support", "non_pro_rata_terms",
          "control_index", "ownership_index", "runway_index"]:
    d = pr2.dropna(subset=[f])
    m = smf.ols(f"{f} ~ structural + mixed + C(year) + C(industry)", data=d) \
           .fit(cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": d["company"]})
    ci = m.conf_int().loc["structural"]
    rows.append(dict(term=f, n=int(m.nobs), share_A=d[d.cause_group == "A"][f].mean(), share_B=d[d.cause_group == "B"][f].mean(),
                     B_minus_A=m.params["structural"], se=m.bse["structural"], p=m.pvalues["structural"],
                     ci_low=ci[0], ci_high=ci[1], C_minus_A=m.params["mixed"], p_C=m.pvalues["mixed"]))
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("term").round(3)

new.name: S2-3b
new.text: Regressing each term separately, the structural-minus-shock difference is small and insignificant for every one of them (haircut +0.10, p = 0.40; documents tightened +0.10, p = 0.41; equity control +0.03, p = 0.68), so the weak index result above is five small positives adding up rather than any single term lenders condition on. With 42 shock and 71 structural deals the smallest difference this sample could reliably detect is roughly 25–35 percentage points, so the right reading is "no detectable screening," not "no screening": whatever cause-based adjustment lenders make is far smaller than the 24-point gap in two-year failure it would need to offset.

upd.S2-1: Structural firms are not visibly getting tougher terms than shock firms — haircut 44% vs 39%, control transfer 10% vs 10%, documents tightened 33% vs 32% — though note the mixed (C) group gets equity control and governance rights about twice as often.
upd.S2-3: With year and industry fixed effects the structural coefficient on the control index is +0.33 (p = 0.10, 95% CI roughly −0.06 to +0.71) and on documents-tightened +0.10 (p = 0.41): weak evidence that lenders demand somewhat more from structural borrowers, but a modest real effect is not ruled out — see the term-by-term table below.
